title: Dr. Fiona Hill - What's Next for the Russia-Ukraine War  | Prof G Conversations
channel: The Prof G Pod – Scott Galloway
summary: Fiona Hill on the Russia-Ukraine war in 2025: Russia backed by China, Iran and North Korea, sabotage across Europe, New START expiring, and Europe needing to defend itself.

assertions.quote: China, North Korea and Iran have come in on Russia's side
a North Korean troops uh fighting against Ukrainians on the Russian side

verdicts.note: The Bulletin refers to North Korea sending soldiers to fight for Russia in the war against Ukraine.
DDIS: North Korea has sent soldiers to Russia's war and workers to its military industry, besides ammunition and missiles.
US intelligence describes North Korean troops participating in combat operations against Ukraine.
In November 2024 the US readout condemned the deployment of thousands of North Korean troops to Russia as a dangerous expansion of the war against Ukraine; it shows the deployment, not the fighting.

assertions.quote: the GRU, the Russian military intelligence are being um held responsible for arson attacks at shopping centers in Poland and also in Lithuania
Putin is not prepared at all to concede uh beyond the goals that he laid out at the beginning of this conflict

verdicts.note: Russia's public demands in the 2025 talks (four regions, neutrality, limits on Ukraine's army) matched its 2022 aims.

DDIS (Dec 2025) sees no sign Russia will make meaningful compromises: it will accept a ceasefire only if the vast majority of its demands are met, and officials hint at annexing Mykolaiv and Odesa too.
EFIS (Feb 2026) says Russia still pursues Ukraine's complete subjugation and sets long-term operational objectives, using talks only to formalise Ukraine's defeat.
US intelligence says Moscow is confident it will force a settlement on its terms and seeks to restore influence in the former Soviet space, particularly Ukraine, without calling its aims maximalist.

assertions.quote: immediately um you know look for some pretext to violate it again and put the blame on uh Europe or on the Ukrainians

verdicts.note: A forecast of behaviour; Russia broke the Minsk ceasefires, but no general ceasefire has existed to test it.

assertions.quote: The Biden administration extended it, but it expires now in 2026.

verdicts.note: New START was extended to 5 February 2026 and allows no further extension.
SIPRI records New START's expiry in February 2026.

assertions.quote: Putin's lowered the threshold for at least rhetorically talking about using nuclear weapons

verdicts.note: Russia made nuclear threats in 2022 and revised its doctrine in November 2024 to widen the conditions for use.

assertions.quote: if you don't have a nuclear weapon and you don't have a guarantee by a nuclear power, you're in big trouble.

verdicts.note: Public support for nuclear weapons has risen in South Korea and elsewhere, but no new state has begun a weapons program.

assertions.quote: We're not going to um give article 5 guarantees to Europe unless it's article 5%.

verdicts.note: Trump has made defence conditional on spending and US strategy deprioritises Europe, though US forces and Article 5 remain formally in place.
Brzezinski cites the Trump administration's determination to dilute US military commitment to and leadership in NATO, and 39% of respondents do not expect the US to keep its central role by 2036.
SIPRI's director names the 'fraying of the USA's relationships with its allies' as a main driver of insecurity; this shows strained relations and doubts, not a formally weakened commitment.
DDIS reports growing uncertainty about the US role as primary guarantor of European security as it prioritises China and the Western Hemisphere, but does not say the commitment has been withdrawn.
Eurasia Group describes a security vacuum in Europe left by America's retreat.
The Munich Security Report cites Washington's gradual retreat, wavering support for Ukraine and threats over Greenland, and calls the US approach to European security volatile.

assertions.quote: take their defense spending from 1.9 to 3%, which they've stated, quite frankly, they don't need the Americans.

verdicts.note: Europe's economy dwarfs Russia's, but it lacks US enablers (intelligence, airlift, air defence) and needs years to replace them.
European NATO members spent $559 billion in 2025, nearly three times Russia's estimated $190 billion at market rates; spending alone does not show industrial capacity or readiness without the US.

assertions.quote: They see this as a proxy war against the United States. And so, they don't want to see Russia lose.

verdicts.note: China's motives are not on the public record, though its support for Russia's war economy is documented.
DoD says the partnership is 'almost certainly driven by a shared interest in countering the United States', but it does not say Beijing sees the Ukraine war itself as a proxy war against the US.
DDIS says China has a vested interest in the Russia-West conflict persisting because it diverts US attention from China, close to but not the same as seeing it as a proxy war.
